evidence.quote: Day-old loaves go to half price at two in the afternoon, not at close. At close nobody is left to buy them.

observations.why: Ines asserts an operational policy rule while backing it immediately with logical commercial justification ('At close nobody is left to buy them').

evidence.quote: Then the shelf card changes at two as well, so the price is never a surprise at the till.

observations.why: Caleb builds on the procedure using rational-persuasion ('so the price is never a surprise at the till') to justify operational synchronization.
